summary: 089 fixes the current missing-Verification path: next() now blocks instead of returning review-apply. However, the gate still tests only Verification fact availability. The approved D1 contract requires facts to be both available and passed. The implementation has no passed-state predicate or status result, so a future C1 snapshot with Verification=failed or not-run would be treated as available and incorrectly allow review-apply and the approved-review archive path. Existing tests cover only today's unavailable snapshot and therefore miss this semantic defect.

blockingFindings.title: Verification gate conflates fact availability with a passed result
blockingFindings.problem: The only predicate is isVerificationFactAvailable(). Its documented future behavior is to return true when a Verification field exists, and both canRun(review-apply) and next() treat true as sufficient. No predicate or result checks that Verification is passed. The same availability-only check controls the approved-review archive path.
blockingFindings.evidence: The approved specification requires review-apply facts to be available and passed (spec.md:178-184, 209-215), and distinguishes unavailable from available-but-failed and available-but-not-run (spec.md:382-391). 088's required change also required a future-compatible review-apply case only when Verification is both available and passed. In 089, next.ts calls only isVerificationFactAvailable; preconditions.ts documents that function as availability rather than passed status; no test exercises failed/not-run or a passed gate.
blockingFindings.impact: The current C1 snapshot remains safely blocked, but the documented future extension would make any present Verification field—including failed or not-run—eligible for review-apply and could then progress an approved review toward archive. This violates the fail-closed Verification contract at the extension boundary.
blockingFindings.requiredChange: Represent the Verification gate as a status-aware, fail-closed predicate/result used consistently by canRun and next. In D1 it must remain unavailable because C1 exposes no status; when the snapshot is extended, only passed may permit review-apply or archive, while not-run and failed produce their distinct blocked diagnoses. Update the current unavailable tests and add status-result coverage at the gate boundary; do not infer status from Run history, OpenSpec artifacts, or chat.
